load_config_file.description: Whether to load YAML/JSON CMS configuration file(s) when [manually initializing the CMS](https://sveltiacms.app/en/docs/api/initialization). This works only in the `CMS.init()` method’s `config` option. Default: `true`.
load_config_file.markdownDescription: Whether to load YAML/JSON CMS configuration file(s) when [manually initializing the CMS](https://sveltiacms.app/en/docs/api/initialization). This works only in the `CMS.init()` method’s `config` option. Default: `true`.

publish_mode.description: Publish mode, or an object with the publish mode and its options. An empty string is the same as `simple`. Default: `simple`. It can be overridden for each collection with the collection-level `publish_mode` option. Note that Editorial Workflow and Preview Workflow are currently supported with the GitHub, GitLab and Gitea/Forgejo backends only. See the [documentation](https://sveltiacms.app/en/docs/workflows) for details.
publish_mode.markdownDescription: Publish mode, or an object with the publish mode and its options. An empty string is the same as `simple`. Default: `simple`. It can be overridden for each collection with the collection-level `publish_mode` option. Note that Editorial Workflow and Preview Workflow are currently supported with the GitHub, GitLab and Gitea/Forgejo backends only. See the [documentation](https://sveltiacms.app/en/docs/workflows) for details.

media_folder.description: Global internal media folder path, relative to the project’s root directory. Required unless a cloud media storage is configured.
media_folder.markdownDescription: Global internal media folder path, relative to the project’s root directory. Required unless a cloud media storage is configured.

public_folder.description: Global public media folder path, relative to the project’s public URL, e.g. `/images/uploads`. A leading slash is added if missing, while a relative path starting with `./` or `../` and a full URL are not allowed. Default: `/` followed by the `media_folder` option value.
public_folder.markdownDescription: Global public media folder path, relative to the project’s public URL, e.g. `/images/uploads`. A leading slash is added if missing, while a relative path starting with `./` or `../` and a full URL are not allowed. Default: `/` followed by the `media_folder` option value.

name.description: Library name. Default: `default`, the internal media storage.
name.markdownDescription: Library name. Default: `default`, the internal media storage.

config.description: Configuration for the default media storage.
config.markdownDescription: Configuration for the default media storage.

name.description: Library name. Default: `default`, the internal media storage.
name.markdownDescription: Library name. Default: `default`, the internal media storage.

output_filename_only.description: Whether to output a file name instead of a full URL. Default: `false`.
output_filename_only.markdownDescription: Whether to output a file name instead of a full URL. Default: `false`.

use_transformations.description: Whether to include transformation segments in an output URL. Default: `true`.
use_transformations.markdownDescription: Whether to include transformation segments in an output URL. Default: `true`.

config.description: Options to be passed to the Cloudinary Media Library widget, such as `multiple`, `max_files`, `default_transformations` and `folder`. The `cloud_name` and `api_key` options are required. A field-level `config` is merged over the site-level one, so the credentials only need to be set at the site level. See the [Cloudinary documentation](https://cloudinary.com/documentation/media_library_widget#2_set_the_configuration_options) for a full list of available options. The `multiple` option is overridden by the field’s own `multiple` option, and `max_files` by the field’s `max` option. Default `max_files`: `20`.
config.markdownDescription: Options to be passed to the Cloudinary Media Library widget, such as `multiple`, `max_files`, `default_transformations` and `folder`. The `cloud_name` and `api_key` options are required. A field-level `config` is merged over the site-level one, so the credentials only need to be set at the site level. See the [Cloudinary documentation](https://cloudinary.com/documentation/media_library_widget#2_set_the_configuration_options) for a full list of available options. The `multiple` option is overridden by the field’s own `multiple` option, and `max_files` by the field’s `max` option. Default `max_files`: `20`.

name.description: Library name. Default: `default`, the internal media storage.
name.markdownDescription: Library name. Default: `default`, the internal media storage.

config.description: Options to be passed to Uploadcare, such as `multiple`. The `publicKey` option is required. A field-level `config` is merged over the site-level one, so the key can be set at either the site or field level. The `cdnBase` option sets the CDN origin used in output URLs. Default: the origin of the file URL returned by Uploadcare, typically `https://ucarecdn.com`. See the [Uploadcare documentation](https://uploadcare.com/docs/uploads/file-uploader-options/) for a full list of available options. Some options, including `previewStep`, will be ignored in Sveltia CMS because we use an API-based integration instead of Uploadcare’s deprecated jQuery File Uploader.
config.markdownDescription: Options to be passed to Uploadcare, such as `multiple`. The `publicKey` option is required. A field-level `config` is merged over the site-level one, so the key can be set at either the site or field level. The `cdnBase` option sets the CDN origin used in output URLs. Default: the origin of the file URL returned by Uploadcare, typically `https://ucarecdn.com`. See the [Uploadcare documentation](https://uploadcare.com/docs/uploads/file-uploader-options/) for a full list of available options. Some options, including `previewStep`, will be ignored in Sveltia CMS because we use an API-based integration instead of Uploadcare’s deprecated jQuery File Uploader.

settings.description: Integration settings. Field-level settings are merged over the site-level ones.
settings.markdownDescription: Integration settings. Field-level settings are merged over the site-level ones.

name.description: Library name. Default: `default`, the internal media storage.
name.markdownDescription: Library name. Default: `default`, the internal media storage.

access_key_id.description: AWS access key ID or equivalent (safe to store in config). Required for all services except Bunny Storage, where it defaults to `bucket`, as the storage zone name serves as the access key ID.
access_key_id.markdownDescription: AWS access key ID or equivalent (safe to store in config). Required for all services except Bunny Storage, where it defaults to `bucket`, as the storage zone name serves as the access key ID.

bucket.description: Bucket name. For Bunny Storage, this is the storage zone name.
bucket.markdownDescription: Bucket name. For Bunny Storage, this is the storage zone name.

region.description: Region, e.g. `us-east-1`. Required for Amazon S3, Backblaze B2, Bunny Storage (two-letter storage region code, e.g. `de`), DigitalOcean Spaces and Scaleway Object Storage. For Supabase Storage, set it to the project’s region; it defaults to `us-east-1`. Ignored for Cloudflare R2, which always uses `auto`. With a custom `endpoint`, it’s only used to sign requests and must match the server’s region, e.g. Garage’s `s3_region` (`garage` by default) or MinIO’s `us-east-1`; otherwise every request fails with a signature mismatch.
region.markdownDescription: Region, e.g. `us-east-1`. Required for Amazon S3, Backblaze B2, Bunny Storage (two-letter storage region code, e.g. `de`), DigitalOcean Spaces and Scaleway Object Storage. For Supabase Storage, set it to the project’s region; it defaults to `us-east-1`. Ignored for Cloudflare R2, which always uses `auto`. With a custom `endpoint`, it’s only used to sign requests and must match the server’s region, e.g. Garage’s `s3_region` (`garage` by default) or MinIO’s `us-east-1`; otherwise every request fails with a signature mismatch.

account_id.description: Cloudflare account ID. Required for Cloudflare R2.
account_id.markdownDescription: Cloudflare account ID. Required for Cloudflare R2.

jurisdiction.description: Cloudflare R2 jurisdiction. Required for buckets created in the EU or FedRAMP jurisdictions; the global endpoint returns an error for those buckets. Default: `'default'`.
jurisdiction.markdownDescription: Cloudflare R2 jurisdiction. Required for buckets created in the EU or FedRAMP jurisdictions; the global endpoint returns an error for those buckets. Default: `'default'`.

project_id.description: Supabase project reference ID. Required for Supabase Storage.
project_id.markdownDescription: Supabase project reference ID. Required for Supabase Storage.

endpoint.description: Custom endpoint URL for another S3-compatible service, such as a self-hosted Garage or MinIO server, configured as `aws_s3`, e.g. `https://s3.example.com`. Objects are addressed with path-style URLs (`{endpoint}/{bucket}/{key}`), so no wildcard DNS is needed. Ignored for the other services, whose endpoints are derived from their own options.
endpoint.markdownDescription: Custom endpoint URL for another S3-compatible service, such as a self-hosted Garage or MinIO server, configured as `aws_s3`, e.g. `https://s3.example.com`. Objects are addressed with path-style URLs (`{endpoint}/{bucket}/{key}`), so no wildcard DNS is needed. Ignored for the other services, whose endpoints are derived from their own options.

prefix.description: Path prefix within the bucket, e.g. `uploads/`. A trailing slash is added if missing.
prefix.markdownDescription: Path prefix within the bucket, e.g. `uploads/`. A trailing slash is added if missing.

force_path_style.description: Whether to use path-style URLs (`https://s3.region.amazonaws.com/bucket/key`) instead of virtual-hosted-style URLs (`https://bucket.s3.region.amazonaws.com/key`) for Amazon S3. Path-style URLs are always used with a custom `endpoint`. Default: `false`.
force_path_style.markdownDescription: Whether to use path-style URLs (`https://s3.region.amazonaws.com/bucket/key`) instead of virtual-hosted-style URLs (`https://bucket.s3.region.amazonaws.com/key`) for Amazon S3. Path-style URLs are always used with a custom `endpoint`. Default: `false`.

public_url.description: Base URL for public asset access. When set, asset preview and download URLs are constructed as `{public_url}/{key}` instead of the S3 API endpoint URL. Required for Cloudflare R2 (S3 API endpoint always requires authentication); set to the `r2.dev` development URL (e.g. `https://pub-abcd1234.r2.dev`) or a custom domain. Also required for Bunny Storage; set to the hostname of a pull zone connected to the storage zone (e.g. `https://my-zone.b-cdn.net`) or a custom domain. Optional for Amazon S3 and DigitalOcean Spaces — use when serving assets through a CDN or custom domain (e.g. CloudFront or Route 53 for S3, CDN endpoint for Spaces). Backblaze B2, DigitalOcean Spaces, Scaleway Object Storage and Supabase Storage have a default public URL derived from the other options.
public_url.markdownDescription: Base URL for public asset access. When set, asset preview and download URLs are constructed as `{public_url}/{key}` instead of the S3 API endpoint URL. Required for Cloudflare R2 (S3 API endpoint always requires authentication); set to the `r2.dev` development URL (e.g. `https://pub-abcd1234.r2.dev`) or a custom domain. Also required for Bunny Storage; set to the hostname of a pull zone connected to the storage zone (e.g. `https://my-zone.b-cdn.net`) or a custom domain. Optional for Amazon S3 and DigitalOcean Spaces — use when serving assets through a CDN or custom domain (e.g. CloudFront or Route 53 for S3, CDN endpoint for Spaces). Backblaze B2, DigitalOcean Spaces, Scaleway Object Storage and Supabase Storage have a default public URL derived from the other options.

name.description: Library name. Default: `default`, the internal media storage.
name.markdownDescription: Library name. Default: `default`, the internal media storage.

account_name.description: Storage account name. Required unless `endpoint` is given.
account_name.markdownDescription: Storage account name. Required unless `endpoint` is given.

endpoint.description: Custom Blob service endpoint including the account, such as a custom domain or the Azurite emulator URL. Overrides `account_name`.
endpoint.markdownDescription: Custom Blob service endpoint including the account, such as a custom domain or the Azurite emulator URL. Overrides `account_name`.

prefix.description: Path prefix within the container, e.g. `uploads/`. A trailing slash is added if missing.
prefix.markdownDescription: Path prefix within the container, e.g. `uploads/`. A trailing slash is added if missing.

public_url.description: Base URL for public asset access. When set, asset download URLs are constructed as `{public_url}/{blob_name}` instead of the Blob service URL. Required unless the container allows anonymous read access, because the URL stored in an entry can’t contain the SAS token, which expires. Set it to an Azure CDN or Front Door endpoint, or a custom domain.
public_url.markdownDescription: Base URL for public asset access. When set, asset download URLs are constructed as `{public_url}/{blob_name}` instead of the Blob service URL. Required unless the container allows anonymous read access, because the URL stored in an entry can’t contain the SAS token, which expires. Set it to an Azure CDN or Front Door endpoint, or a custom domain.

name.description: Library name. Default: `default`, the internal media storage.
name.markdownDescription: Library name. Default: `default`, the internal media storage.

providers.description: Enabled stock photo/video providers. The stock photo/video section in the asset browser is hidden if an empty array is given. Default: all supported providers.
providers.markdownDescription: Enabled stock photo/video providers. The stock photo/video section in the asset browser is hidden if an empty array is given. Default: all supported providers.

media_library.description: Legacy media storage option that allows only one library. Use `media_libraries` instead to support multiple storage providers. If both options define the same library, `media_libraries` takes precedence.
media_library.markdownDescription: Legacy media storage option that allows only one library. Use `media_libraries` instead to support multiple storage providers. If both options define the same library, `media_libraries` takes precedence.

media_libraries.description: Unified media storage option that supports multiple libraries. See the [documentation](https://sveltiacms.app/en/docs/media#configuration) for details.
media_libraries.markdownDescription: Unified media storage option that supports multiple libraries. See the [documentation](https://sveltiacms.app/en/docs/media#configuration) for details.

app_title.description: Custom title for the CMS, which will be displayed on the login page and the browser’s tab. Default: `Sveltia CMS`.
app_title.markdownDescription: Custom title for the CMS, which will be displayed on the login page and the browser’s tab. Default: `Sveltia CMS`.

site_url.description: Site URL. Default: current site’s origin ([`location.origin`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Location/origin)).
site_url.markdownDescription: Site URL. Default: current site’s origin ([`location.origin`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Location/origin)).

display_url.description: Site URL linked from the UI. Default: `site_url` option value.
display_url.markdownDescription: Site URL linked from the UI. Default: `site_url` option value.

logo_url.description: Absolute URL or absolute path to the site logo that will be displayed on the entrance page and the browser’s tab (favicon). A square image works best. Default: Sveltia logo.
logo_url.markdownDescription: Absolute URL or absolute path to the site logo that will be displayed on the entrance page and the browser’s tab (favicon). A square image works best. Default: Sveltia logo.
logo_url.deprecationMessage: This option is superseded by the new `logo.src` option. See the documentation https://sveltiacms.app/en/docs/customization#custom-logo for details.

logout_redirect_url.description: URL to redirect users to after logging out. Default: none, so users stay on the CMS sign-in page.
logout_redirect_url.markdownDescription: URL to redirect users to after logging out. Default: none, so users stay on the CMS sign-in page.

issue_reports.description: Issue reporting options. Accepted for compatibility with Decap CMS but ignored.
issue_reports.markdownDescription: Issue reporting options. Accepted for compatibility with Decap CMS but ignored.

show_preview_links.description: Whether to show links to entries on the live site and on deploy previews. Default: `true`.
show_preview_links.markdownDescription: Whether to show links to entries on the live site and on deploy previews. Default: `true`.

slug.description: Slug options, which apply to entry slugs and to the names of entry folders created or renamed in a nested collection. They also apply to uploaded asset file names and new asset folder names if the `slugify_filename` media library option is enabled.
slug.markdownDescription: Slug options, which apply to entry slugs and to the names of entry folders created or renamed in a nested collection. They also apply to uploaded asset file names and new asset folder names if the `slugify_filename` media library option is enabled.

collections.description: Set of collections. The list can also contain dividers, which are used to group collections in the collection list. Either `collections` or `singletons` option must be defined.
collections.markdownDescription: Set of collections. The list can also contain dividers, which are used to group collections in the collection list. Either `collections` or `singletons` option must be defined.

singletons.description: Set of singleton files, such as the CMS configuration file or the homepage file. They are not part of any collection and can be accessed directly through the collection list. The list can also contain dividers. See the [documentation](https://sveltiacms.app/en/docs/collections/singletons) for details.
singletons.markdownDescription: Set of singleton files, such as the CMS configuration file or the homepage file. They are not part of any collection and can be accessed directly through the collection list. The list can also contain dividers. See the [documentation](https://sveltiacms.app/en/docs/collections/singletons) for details.

i18n.description: Global i18n options.
i18n.markdownDescription: Global i18n options.

output.description: Data output options. See the [documentation](https://sveltiacms.app/en/docs/data-output#controlling-data-output) for details.
output.markdownDescription: Data output options. See the [documentation](https://sveltiacms.app/en/docs/data-output#controlling-data-output) for details.

readonly.description: Whether to make the whole CMS read-only, e.g. while the site is under maintenance. Default: `false`. All the collections, files and asset folders can be viewed but not changed, as if they all had the `readonly` option set to `true`. Collections and files can also be made read-only individually with their own `readonly` option.
readonly.markdownDescription: Whether to make the whole CMS read-only, e.g. while the site is under maintenance. Default: `false`. All the collections, files and asset folders can be viewed but not changed, as if they all had the `readonly` option set to `true`. Collections and files can also be made read-only individually with their own `readonly` option.

name.description: Backend name.
name.markdownDescription: Backend name.

repo.description: Repository identifier: organization/user name and repository name joined by a slash, e.g. `owner/repo`.
repo.markdownDescription: Repository identifier: organization/user name and repository name joined by a slash, e.g. `owner/repo`.

api_root.description: REST API endpoint for the backend. Required when using GitHub Enterprise Server, for which `https://HOSTNAME/api/v3` or just `https://HOSTNAME` can be given. Default: `https://api.github.com`.
api_root.markdownDescription: REST API endpoint for the backend. Required when using GitHub Enterprise Server, for which `https://HOSTNAME/api/v3` or just `https://HOSTNAME` can be given. Default: `https://api.github.com`.

graphql_api_root.description: GraphQL API endpoint for the backend. Default: inferred from the `api_root` option value: `https://api.github.com/graphql` for GitHub.com, and `https://HOSTNAME/api/graphql` for GitHub Enterprise Server.
graphql_api_root.markdownDescription: GraphQL API endpoint for the backend. Default: inferred from the `api_root` option value: `https://api.github.com/graphql` for GitHub.com, and `https://HOSTNAME/api/graphql` for GitHub Enterprise Server.

base_url.description: OAuth base URL origin. Required when using an OAuth client other than Netlify, including [Sveltia CMS Authenticator](https://github.com/sveltia/sveltia-cms-auth). Default: `https://api.netlify.com`.
base_url.markdownDescription: OAuth base URL origin. Required when using an OAuth client other than Netlify, including [Sveltia CMS Authenticator](https://github.com/sveltia/sveltia-cms-auth). Default: `https://api.netlify.com`.

auth_type.description: OAuth grant type. The default is an empty string, which is authorization code grant. `pkce` is not yet supported due to GitHub’s limitations.
auth_type.markdownDescription: OAuth grant type. The default is an empty string, which is authorization code grant. `pkce` is not yet supported due to GitHub’s limitations.

app_id.description: OAuth application ID. Not used at this time; reserved for PKCE authorization, which is not yet supported with GitHub.
app_id.markdownDescription: OAuth application ID. Not used at this time; reserved for PKCE authorization, which is not yet supported with GitHub.

cms_label_prefix.description: Pull request label prefix used when writing Editorial Workflow labels. Default: `sveltia-cms/`. When reading labels, the `sveltia-cms/`, `netlify-cms/` and `decap-cms/` prefixes are also recognized, so unpublished entries created with a different prefix or with Netlify/Decap CMS remain editable.
cms_label_prefix.markdownDescription: Pull request label prefix used when writing Editorial Workflow labels. Default: `sveltia-cms/`. When reading labels, the `sveltia-cms/`, `netlify-cms/` and `decap-cms/` prefixes are also recognized, so unpublished entries created with a different prefix or with Netlify/Decap CMS remain editable.

squash_merges.description: Whether to use squash merge for Editorial Workflow. Default: `false`.
squash_merges.markdownDescription: Whether to use squash merge for Editorial Workflow. Default: `false`.

preview_context.description: Name of the commit status context or deployment environment that carries the deploy preview URL, matched as a case-insensitive substring. Default: any context or environment that looks like a deploy preview. See the [documentation](https://sveltiacms.app/en/docs/workflows/deploy-previews) for details.
preview_context.markdownDescription: Name of the commit status context or deployment environment that carries the deploy preview URL, matched as a case-insensitive substring. Default: any context or environment that looks like a deploy preview. See the [documentation](https://sveltiacms.app/en/docs/workflows/deploy-previews) for details.

open_authoring.description: Whether to enable Open Authoring, which lets a contributor without write access to the repository propose changes from a fork. It requires the `editorial_workflow` publish mode. Default: `false`. See the [documentation](https://sveltiacms.app/en/docs/workflows/open) for details.
open_authoring.markdownDescription: Whether to enable Open Authoring, which lets a contributor without write access to the repository propose changes from a fork. It requires the `editorial_workflow` publish mode. Default: `false`. See the [documentation](https://sveltiacms.app/en/docs/workflows/open) for details.

auth_scope.description: OAuth scope to request when signing in, or a list of scopes, which must include `repo` or `public_repo`. Default: `repo`. With Open Authoring on a public repository, `public_repo` is enough and asks the contributor for a narrower grant. A private repository always needs `repo`. Adding `workflow` lets the CMS keep a contributor’s fork in sync when your GitHub Actions workflow files change, at the cost of letting the token change workflows in every repository the contributor can push to. See the [documentation](https://sveltiacms.app/en/docs/workflows/open#authentication-scope) for details.
auth_scope.markdownDescription: OAuth scope to request when signing in, or a list of scopes, which must include `repo` or `public_repo`. Default: `repo`. With Open Authoring on a public repository, `public_repo` is enough and asks the contributor for a narrower grant. A private repository always needs `repo`. Adding `workflow` lets the CMS keep a contributor’s fork in sync when your GitHub Actions workflow files change, at the cost of letting the token change workflows in every repository the contributor can push to. See the [documentation](https://sveltiacms.app/en/docs/workflows/open#authentication-scope) for details.

branch.description: Git branch name. If omitted, the default branch, usually `main` or `master`, will be automatically detected and used.
branch.markdownDescription: Git branch name. If omitted, the default branch, usually `main` or `master`, will be automatically detected and used.

root_dir.description: Directory in the repository that the CMS treats as the root, such as the directory of a site in a monorepo, e.g. `apps/blog`. Every path in the configuration, like a collection’s `folder` or the `media_folder`, is then relative to this directory, and files outside it are not shown. Editorial Workflow branches are named after it as well, so the sites in a monorepo don’t share them; with Editorial Workflow, no part of the path can start with a dot, end with `.lock` or contain a space or a character Git doesn’t allow in a branch name, such as `:` or `*`. Default: the repository root. See the [documentation](https://sveltiacms.app/en/docs/backends#monorepos) for details.
root_dir.markdownDescription: Directory in the repository that the CMS treats as the root, such as the directory of a site in a monorepo, e.g. `apps/blog`. Every path in the configuration, like a collection’s `folder` or the `media_folder`, is then relative to this directory, and files outside it are not shown. Editorial Workflow branches are named after it as well, so the sites in a monorepo don’t share them; with Editorial Workflow, no part of the path can start with a dot, end with `.lock` or contain a space or a character Git doesn’t allow in a branch name, such as `:` or `*`. Default: the repository root. See the [documentation](https://sveltiacms.app/en/docs/backends#monorepos) for details.

site_domain.description: Site domain used for OAuth, which will be included in the `site_id` param to be sent to the API endpoint. Default: [current hostname](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Location/hostname) (or `cms.netlify.com` on `localhost`).
site_domain.markdownDescription: Site domain used for OAuth, which will be included in the `site_id` param to be sent to the API endpoint. Default: [current hostname](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Location/hostname) (or `cms.netlify.com` on `localhost`).

automatic_deployments.description: Whether to enable or disable automatic deployments with any connected CI/CD provider. Default: `undefined`.
automatic_deployments.markdownDescription: Whether to enable or disable automatic deployments with any connected CI/CD provider. Default: `undefined`.
automatic_deployments.deprecationMessage: Use the new `skip_ci` option instead, which is more intuitive. `automatic_deployments: false` is equivalent to `skip_ci: true`, and `automatic_deployments: true` is equivalent to `skip_ci: false`. See the documentation https://sveltiacms.app/en/docs/deployments#disabling-automatic-deployments for details.

skip_ci.description: Whether to enable or disable automatic deployments with any connected CI/CD provider, such as GitHub Actions or Cloudflare Pages. If `true`, the `[skip ci]` prefix will be added to commit messages, except for deletions. Setting it to either `true` or `false` also lets users trigger a deployment manually and toggle the prefix for each save. Default: `undefined`. See the [documentation](https://sveltiacms.app/en/docs/deployments#disabling-automatic-deployments) for details.
skip_ci.markdownDescription: Whether to enable or disable automatic deployments with any connected CI/CD provider, such as GitHub Actions or Cloudflare Pages. If `true`, the `[skip ci]` prefix will be added to commit messages, except for deletions. Setting it to either `true` or `false` also lets users trigger a deployment manually and toggle the prefix for each save. Default: `undefined`. See the [documentation](https://sveltiacms.app/en/docs/deployments#disabling-automatic-deployments) for details.

prompt_commit_messages.description: Whether to ask the user for a commit message every time changes are committed. If `true`, the user can replace the message made from the `commit_messages` template, which the text box is filled in with. If `prefix` or `suffix`, the text the user enters, e.g. an issue number, is added before or after that message, with a space in between. The message made from the template is used as is if the text box is left empty. Default: `false`. See the [documentation](https://sveltiacms.app/en/docs/backends#commit-messages) for details.
prompt_commit_messages.markdownDescription: Whether to ask the user for a commit message every time changes are committed. If `true`, the user can replace the message made from the `commit_messages` template, which the text box is filled in with. If `prefix` or `suffix`, the text the user enters, e.g. an issue number, is added before or after that message, with a space in between. The message made from the template is used as is if the text box is left empty. Default: `false`. See the [documentation](https://sveltiacms.app/en/docs/backends#commit-messages) for details.

auth_methods.description: Allowed authentication methods. Default: both `oauth` and `token` are allowed. To restrict sign-in options, specify only the methods you want to enable, e.g. `[oauth]` to disable access token sign-in, or `[token]` to disable OAuth sign-in. An empty array is invalid and will result in a configuration error.
auth_methods.markdownDescription: Allowed authentication methods. Default: both `oauth` and `token` are allowed. To restrict sign-in options, specify only the methods you want to enable, e.g. `[oauth]` to disable access token sign-in, or `[token]` to disable OAuth sign-in. include_credentials.description: Whether to include credentials in API requests. Default: `false`. If set to `true`, credentials such as cookies will be included in API requests. This is only necessary when using cookie-based authentication with a self-hosted Git backend.

root_dir.description: Directory in the repository that the CMS treats as the root, such as the directory of a site in a monorepo, e.g. `apps/blog`. Every path in the configuration, like a collection’s `folder` or the `media_folder`, is then relative to this directory, and files outside it are not shown. PublishModeType.description: Publish mode. `simple` commits each change to the configured branch right away. `preview` saves each change to a pull request, so it can be previewed on a deploy preview before it’s published, without any review stages. `editorial_workflow` saves each change to a pull request that moves through review stages before it can be published.

type.description: Publish mode. Default: `simple` at the global level, and the global publish mode at the collection level.
type.markdownDescription: Publish mode. Default: `simple` at the global level, and the global publish mode at the collection level.

stages.description: Review stages an unpublished entry moves through, in order. The list must start with `draft`. An entry can be published once it reaches the last stage, so `[draft, pending_publish]` drops the In Review stage. Default: `[draft, pending_review, pending_publish]`. It only applies to the `editorial_workflow` publish mode.
stages.markdownDescription: Review stages an unpublished entry moves through, in order. The list must start with `draft`. An entry can be published once it reaches the last stage, so `[draft, pending_publish]` drops the In Review stage. Default: `[draft, pending_review, pending_publish]`. It only applies to the `editorial_workflow` publish mode.

direct_publish.description: Whether to let users save and publish an entry in one go, bypassing the review: the change is committed straight to the configured branch, or the entry’s pull request is merged once the change is saved to it. The option is not offered for a collection with `publish: false`, or to an Open Authoring contributor. Default: `false`. It only applies to the `editorial_workflow` and `preview` publish modes.

allow_incomplete_drafts.description: Whether an entry in the `draft` stage can be saved with its required fields left empty. The fields have to be filled in before the entry moves on or is published. Default: `true`. It only applies to the `editorial_workflow` and `preview` publish modes.
allow_incomplete_drafts.markdownDescription: Whether an entry in the `draft` stage can be saved with its required fields left empty. The fields have to be filled in before the entry moves on or is published. Default: `true`. It only applies to the `editorial_workflow` and `preview` publish modes.

max_file_size.markdownDescription: Maximum file size in bytes that can be accepted for uploading. Default: `Infinity`, meaning no limit.

slugify_filename.description: Whether to rename an original asset file when saving it, according to the global `slug` option. Default: `false`, meaning that the original file name is kept by default, while Netlify/Decap CMS forces to slugify file names. If set to `true`, for example, `Hello World (1).webp` would be `hello-world-1.webp`.
slugify_filename.markdownDescription: Whether to rename an original asset file when saving it, according to the global `slug` option. Default: `false`, meaning that the original file name is kept by default, while Netlify/Decap CMS forces to slugify file names. If set to `true`, for example, `Hello World (1).webp` would be `hello-world-1.webp`.

filename_template.description: Template to rename an uploaded file with, like `{{slug}}-{{uuid_short}}`. It supports the same tags and transformations as the entry `slug` option, including `{{slug}}`, `{{fields.title}}`, date/time tags and `{{uuid}}`, as well as `{{filename}}` and `{{extension}}` for the original file name and extension. The extension is always appended, so the template shouldn’t include it. The values of the tags are slugified, and the entry tags are filled with the default locale’s content when the entry is saved. A file uploaded in the asset library or to a cloud storage service is named right away, without an entry, so only the other tags make sense there; Cloudinary keeps the name as the original file name of an asset whose public ID is generated. A file renamed by hand before saving keeps that name, and a file replacing an existing asset takes over its name. Default: `undefined`, meaning that the original file name is kept, or slugified if the `slugify_filename` option is enabled.
filename_template.markdownDescription: Template to rename an uploaded file with, like `{{slug}}-{{uuid_short}}`. It supports the same tags and transformations as the entry `slug` option, including `{{slug}}`, `{{fields.title}}`, date/time tags and `{{uuid}}`, as well as `{{filename}}` and `{{extension}}` for the original file name and extension. The extension is always appended, so the template shouldn’t include it. The values of the tags are slugified, and the entry tags are filled with the default locale’s content when the entry is saved. A file uploaded in the asset library or to a cloud storage service is named right away, without an entry, so only the other tags make sense there; Cloudinary keeps the name as the original file name of an asset whose public ID is generated. A file renamed by hand before saving keeps that name, and a file replacing an existing asset takes over its name. Default: `undefined`, meaning that the original file name is kept, or slugified if the `slugify_filename` option is enabled.

filename_template.description: Template to rename an uploaded file with, like `{{slug}}-{{uuid_short}}`. It supports the same tags and transformations as the entry `slug` option, including `{{slug}}`, `{{fields.title}}`, date/time tags and `{{uuid}}`, as well as `{{filename}}` and `{{extension}}` for the original file name and extension. The extension is always appended, so the template shouldn’t include it. The values of the tags are slugified, and the entry tags are filled with the default locale’s content when the entry is saved. A file uploaded in the asset library or to a cloud storage service is named right away, without an entry, so only the other tags make sense there; Cloudinary keeps the name as the original file name of an asset whose public ID is generated. A file renamed by hand before saving keeps that name, and a file replacing an existing asset takes over its name. Default: `undefined`, meaning that the original file name is kept, or slugified if the `slugify_filename` option is enabled.
filename_template.markdownDescription: Template to rename an uploaded file with, like `{{slug}}-{{uuid_short}}`. It supports the same tags and transformations as the entry `slug` option, including `{{slug}}`, `{{fields.title}}`, date/time tags and `{{uuid}}`, as well as `{{filename}}` and `{{extension}}` for the original file name and extension. The extension is always appended, so the template shouldn’t include it. The values of the tags are slugified, and the entry tags are filled with the default locale’s content when the entry is saved. A file uploaded in the asset library or to a cloud storage service is named right away, without an entry, so only the other tags make sense there; Cloudinary keeps the name as the original file name of an asset whose public ID is generated. A file renamed by hand before saving keeps that name, and a file replacing an existing asset takes over its name. Default: `undefined`, meaning that the original file name is kept, or slugified if the `slugify_filename` option is enabled.

config.description: Options to be passed to the Cloudinary Media Library widget, such as `multiple`, `max_files`, `default_transformations` and `folder`. The `cloud_name` and `api_key` options are required. A field-level `config` is merged over the site-level one, so the credentials only need to be set at the site level. See the [Cloudinary documentation](https://cloudinary.com/documentation/media_library_widget#2_set_the_configuration_options) for a full list of available options. The `multiple` option is overridden by the field’s own `multiple` option, and `max_files` by the field’s `max` option. Default `max_files`: `20`.

config.description: Options to be passed to Uploadcare, such as `multiple`. The `publicKey` option is required. A field-level `config` is merged over the site-level one, so the key can be set at either the site or field level. The `cdnBase` option sets the CDN origin used in output URLs. Default: the origin of the file URL returned by Uploadcare, typically `https://ucarecdn.com`. See the [Uploadcare documentation](https://uploadcare.com/docs/uploads/file-uploader-options/) for a full list of available options. Some options, including `previewStep`, will be ignored in Sveltia CMS because we use an API-based integration instead of Uploadcare’s deprecated jQuery File Uploader.

bucket.description: Bucket name. For Bunny Storage, this is the storage zone name.
bucket.markdownDescription: Bucket name. For Bunny Storage, this is the storage zone name.

region.description: Region, e.g. `us-east-1`. Required for Amazon S3, Backblaze B2, Bunny Storage (two-letter storage region code, e.g. `de`), DigitalOcean Spaces and Scaleway Object Storage. For Supabase Storage, set it to the project’s region; it defaults to `us-east-1`. Ignored for Cloudflare R2, which always uses `auto`. With a custom `endpoint`, it’s only used to sign requests and must match the server’s region, e.g. Garage’s `s3_region` (`garage` by default) or MinIO’s `us-east-1`; otherwise every request fails with a signature mismatch.

public_url.description: Base URL for public asset access. When set, asset preview and download URLs are constructed as `{public_url}/{key}` instead of the S3 API endpoint URL. Required for Cloudflare R2 (S3 API endpoint always requires authentication); set to the `r2.dev` development URL (e.g. `https://pub-abcd1234.r2.dev`) or a custom domain. Also required for Bunny Storage; set to the hostname of a pull zone connected to the storage zone (e.g. `https://my-zone.b-cdn.net`) or a custom domain. Optional for Amazon S3 and DigitalOcean Spaces — use when serving assets through a CDN or custom domain (e.g. CloudFront or Route 53 for S3, CDN endpoint for Spaces). Backblaze B2, DigitalOcean Spaces, Scaleway Object Storage and Supabase Storage have a default public URL derived from the other options.

AzureMediaLibrary.description: Options for the Azure Blob Storage media library. Unlike the S3-compatible services, which are authorized with an access key pair, the Blob service is accessed with a [shared access signature (SAS)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/storage-sas-overview) token that each user enters in the CMS’s Settings dialog, so no credential belongs in this configuration. The token needs the Read, Write, Create and List permissions on the container, and the storage account needs a [CORS rule](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/storageservices/cross-origin-resource-sharing--cors--support-for-the-azure-storage-services) that allows the `GET`, `PUT` and `OPTIONS` methods along with the `x-ms-blob-type` and `content-type` headers from the CMS’s origin.

Unlike the S3-compatible services, which are authorized with an access key pair, the Blob service is accessed with a [shared access signature (SAS)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/storage-sas-overview) token that each user enters in the CMS’s Settings dialog, so no credential belongs in this configuration. The token needs the Read, Write, Create and List permissions on the container, and the storage account needs a [CORS rule](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/storageservices/cross-origin-resource-sharing--cors--support-for-the-azure-storage-services) that allows the `GET`, `PUT` and `OPTIONS` methods along with the `x-ms-blob-type` and `content-type` headers from the CMS’s origin.

folder.description: Base folder path relative to the project root. It can contain slashes to create subfolders. With i18n enabled, it can also contain the `{{locale}}` placeholder as a whole folder name, like `content/{{locale}}/posts`, to say where each locale’s folder goes. The placeholder takes precedence over the `structure` i18n option: the collection then has one folder per locale wherever the placeholder is, and the `omit_default_locale_from_file_path` option leaves the default locale’s folder out. See the [documentation](https://sveltiacms.app/en/docs/i18n/structures) for details. Either this or the `file` option is required.

The placeholder takes precedence over the `structure` i18n option: the collection then has one folder per locale wherever the placeholder is, and the `omit_default_locale_from_file_path` option leaves the default locale’s folder out. See the [documentation](https://sveltiacms.app/en/docs/i18n/structures) for details. Either this or the `file` option is required.

file.description: Path to a JSON file, relative to the project root, that stores all the entries of the collection as an array of objects, instead of one file per entry in a `folder`. Each object in the array is an entry, and the entries can be reordered with a drag-and-drop UI, which changes the order of the objects in the array. Saving an entry rewrites the whole file. Options that assume one file per entry, like `path`, `slug`, `extension`, `nested` and `index_file`, are not available, and Editorial Workflow is not supported, including a Relation field referring to a collection with Editorial Workflow. With i18n enabled, each object holds all the translations with the `single_file` structure, or the `single_file_default_root` structure if it’s configured; the `{{locale}}` placeholder is not supported. The slug of an entry is its position in the array, so a Relation field referring to the collection must store a field value with the `value_field` option, and the `preview_path` and `thumbnail` options can’t contain the `{{slug}}` tag. Either this or the `folder` option is required.

Options that assume one file per entry, like `path`, `slug`, `extension`, `nested` and `index_file`, are not available, and Editorial Workflow is not supported, including a Relation field referring to a collection with Editorial Workflow. With i18n enabled, each object holds all the translations with the `single_file` structure, or the `single_file_default_root` structure if it’s configured; the `{{locale}}` placeholder is not supported. The slug of an entry is its position in the array, so a Relation field referring to the collection must store a field value with the `value_field` option, and the `preview_path` and `thumbnail` options can’t contain the `{{slug}}` tag. table_columns.description: Columns of the entry list’s table view, each given as a field name or an object with a custom header label, e.g. `[title, date, { field: author.name, label: Author }]`. A field name can also be one of the special keys: `_summary` for the entry summary, `slug`, `commit_author` and `commit_date`, or a template like the `summary` option’s, e.g. `{{locales}}`. The table view is only offered, as the default view of the entry list, if at least one column is given. If none of them can be shown, the entry summary and the sortable fields are shown instead.
table_columns.markdownDescription: Columns of the entry list’s table view, each given as a field name or an object with a custom header label, e.g. `[title, date, { field: author.name, label: Author }]`. A field name can also be one of the special keys: `_summary` for the entry summary, `slug`, `commit_author` and `commit_date`, or a template like the `summary` option’s, e.g. `{{locales}}`. The table view is only offered, as the default view of the entry list, if at least one column is given. If none of them can be shown, the entry summary and the sortable fields are shown instead.

summary_fields.description: An alias of the `table_columns` option for Static CMS compatibility, where `summary` stands for the entry summary. Ignored if `table_columns` is defined.
summary_fields.markdownDescription: An alias of the `table_columns` option for Static CMS compatibility, where `summary` stands for the entry summary. Ignored if `table_columns` is defined.

bulk_edit.description: Whether to allow users to edit the simple top-level fields of many entries at once in a spreadsheet-like table, saving the changes in a single commit. Default: `false`. Like reordering, it writes to the configured branch directly, even if the Editorial Workflow is enabled. An object can be provided instead to choose the fields, e.g. `{ fields: [title, draft] }`.
bulk_edit.markdownDescription: Whether to allow users to edit the simple top-level fields of many entries at once in a spreadsheet-like table, saving the changes in a single commit. Default: `false`. Like reordering, it writes to the configured branch directly, even if the Editorial Workflow is enabled. An object can be provided instead to choose the fields, e.g. `{ fields: [title, draft] }`.

extension.description: File extension. Default: derived from the `format` option value, e.g. `yml` for `yaml` and `txt` for `raw`, or `md` otherwise.
extension.markdownDescription: File extension. Default: derived from the `format` option value, e.g. `yml` for `yaml` and `txt` for `raw`, or `md` otherwise.

identifier_field.description: Field name to be used as the title and slug of an entry. Default: `title`.
identifier_field.markdownDescription: Field name to be used as the title and slug of an entry. Default: `title`.

slug.description: Item slug template, or an object with the template and the options to let users edit the slug. Default: `identifier_field` option value. The template cannot contain slashes; to organize entries in subfolders, use the `path` option instead. It’s possible to [localize the slug](https://sveltiacms.app/en/docs/i18n/slugs#localizing-entry-slugs) or [use a random ID](https://sveltiacms.app/en/docs/collections/entries/slugs#slug-template-tags). The `{{fields._slug}}` and `{{fields._slug | localize}}` tags, which show a slug editor in new entry drafts, are deprecated; use the object form with the `editable` and `i18n` options instead.
slug.markdownDescription: Item slug template, or an object with the template and the options to let users edit the slug. Default: `identifier_field` option value. The template cannot contain slashes; to organize entries in subfolders, use the `path` option instead. It’s possible to [localize the slug](https://sveltiacms.app/en/docs/i18n/slugs#localizing-entry-slugs) or [use a random ID](https://sveltiacms.app/en/docs/collections/entries/slugs#slug-template-tags). The `{{fields._slug}}` and `{{fields._slug | localize}}` tags, which show a slug editor in new entry drafts, are deprecated; use the object form with the `editable` and `i18n` options instead.

slug_length.description: The maximum number of characters allowed for an entry slug. Default: `Infinity`.
slug_length.markdownDescription: The maximum number of characters allowed for an entry slug. Default: `Infinity`.

summary.description: Entry summary template displayed in the entry list, e.g. `{{title}} ({{date | date('YYYY-MM-DD')}})`. Default: the value of the `identifier_field`, `title`, `name` or `label` field, or the first heading in the `body` field.
summary.markdownDescription: Entry summary template displayed in the entry list, e.g. `{{title}} ({{date | date('YYYY-MM-DD')}})`. Default: the value of the `identifier_field`, `title`, `name` or `label` field, or the first heading in the `body` field.

sortable_fields.description: Custom sortable fields. Default: `title`, `name`, `date`, `author` and `description`, or the `identifier_field` in place of `title`, as long as the fields exist. For a Git backend, `commit_author` and `commit_date` are also available, and added to the list if `author` and `date` are not included. See the [documentation](https://sveltiacms.app/en/docs/collections/entries/views#sorting) for details.
sortable_fields.markdownDescription: Custom sortable fields. Default: `title`, `name`, `date`, `author` and `description`, or the `identifier_field` in place of `title`, as long as the fields exist. For a Git backend, `commit_author` and `commit_date` are also available, and added to the list if `author` and `date` are not included. See the [documentation](https://sveltiacms.app/en/docs/collections/entries/views#sorting) for details.

view_filters.description: View filters to be used in the entry list.
view_filters.markdownDescription: View filters to be used in the entry list.

view_groups.description: View groups to be used in the entry list.
view_groups.markdownDescription: View groups to be used in the entry list.

nested.description: Options for a nested collection, which shows the entries in a folder tree and lets the user organize them in subfolders.
nested.markdownDescription: Options for a nested collection, which shows the entries in a folder tree and lets the user organize them in subfolders.

meta.description: Meta data for a nested collection, which enables the entry path editor. It has no effect without the `nested` option.
meta.markdownDescription: Meta data for a nested collection, which enables the entry path editor. It has no effect without the `nested` option.

index_file.description: Index file inclusion options. If `true`, the default index file name is `_index`, which is used for Hugo’s special index file. See the [documentation](https://sveltiacms.app/en/docs/collections/entries/listings#managing-hugo-s-special-index-file) for details.
index_file.markdownDescription: Index file inclusion options. If `true`, the default index file name is `_index`, which is used for Hugo’s special index file. See the [documentation](https://sveltiacms.app/en/docs/collections/entries/listings#managing-hugo-s-special-index-file) for details.

thumbnail.description: Whether to show entry thumbnails in the entry list. Default: `true` (auto-detect image/file fields). Set to `false` to disable, or provide a field key path (e.g., `heroImage.src`) or an array of paths for fallbacks. Supports nested fields with dot notation and wildcards (e.g., `images.*.src`). A value starting with a slash is a file path instead, resolved like an Image field value, which can contain template tags like the `preview_path` option, e.g. `/images/thumbnails/{{slug}}.webp`. Date and time tags are filled from the field named with the `preview_path_date_field` option, or the first DateTime field. An empty array equals `false`.
thumbnail.markdownDescription: Whether to show entry thumbnails in the entry list. Default: `true` (auto-detect image/file fields). Set to `false` to disable, or provide a field key path (e.g., `heroImage.src`) or an array of paths for fallbacks. Supports nested fields with dot notation and wildcards (e.g., `images.*.src`). A value starting with a slash is a file path instead, resolved like an Image field value, which can contain template tags like the `preview_path` option, e.g. `/images/thumbnails/{{slug}}.webp`. Date and time tags are filled from the field named with the `preview_path_date_field` option, or the first DateTime field. An empty array equals `false`.

limit.description: The maximum number of entries that can be created in the collection. Default: `Infinity`.
limit.markdownDescription: The maximum number of entries that can be created in the collection. Default: `Infinity`.

aliases_field.description: Property name used to store URL aliases (redirects) from an entry’s previous paths to its current path. Default: `aliases`, which is what Hugo and Zola support out of the box. When an editor changes an entry’s slug, the entry’s previous path is appended to this property. Set this to `false` to skip the processing. It has no effect unless the `preview_path` option is also defined, because that option is what tells the CMS an entry’s path on the live site. It also has no effect if a field with the same name is defined in the `fields` option, in which case the property is left to the editor to manage.
aliases_field.markdownDescription: Property name used to store URL aliases (redirects) from an entry’s previous paths to its current path. Default: `aliases`, which is what Hugo and Zola support out of the box. When an editor changes an entry’s slug, the entry’s previous path is appended to this property. Set this to `false` to skip the processing. It has no effect unless the `preview_path` option is also defined, because that option is what tells the CMS an entry’s path on the live site. It also has no effect if a field with the same name is defined in the `fields` option, in which case the property is left to the editor to manage.

label_singular.description: Singular UI label. It will be Blog Post if the `label` is Blog Posts, for example. Default: `label` option value.
label_singular.markdownDescription: Singular UI label. It will be Blog Post if the `label` is Blog Posts, for example. Default: `label` option value.

description.description: Short description of the collection to be displayed in the editor UI.
description.markdownDescription: Short description of the collection to be displayed in the editor UI.

media_folder.description: Internal media folder path for the collection. This overrides the global `media_folder` option. It can be a relative path from the project root if it starts with a slash. Otherwise it’s a path relative to the entry, or to the file for a file collection. If this option is omitted, the global `media_folder` option value is used, except for an entry collection with the `path` option, where the entry’s own folder is used. See the [documentation](https://sveltiacms.app/en/docs/media/internal#collection-level-configuration) for details.
media_folder.markdownDescription: Internal media folder path for the collection. This overrides the global `media_folder` option. It can be a relative path from the project root if it starts with a slash. Otherwise it’s a path relative to the entry, or to the file for a file collection. If this option is omitted, the global `media_folder` option value is used, except for an entry collection with the `path` option, where the entry’s own folder is used. See the [documentation](https://sveltiacms.app/en/docs/media/internal#collection-level-configuration) for details.

public_folder.description: Public media folder path for the collection. This overrides the global `public_folder` option. Default: `media_folder` option value.
public_folder.markdownDescription: Public media folder path for the collection. This overrides the global `public_folder` option. Default: `media_folder` option value.

hide.description: Whether to hide the collection in the UI. Default: `false`.
hide.markdownDescription: Whether to hide the collection in the UI. Default: `false`.

publish_mode.description: Publish mode for the collection. This overrides the global `publish_mode` option, so Editorial Workflow can be enabled for some collections only, or turned off for a collection when it’s enabled globally. In the object form, each option overrides the global one of the same name, and the others are inherited. Default: global `publish_mode` option value. Note that a contributor working on a fork with Open Authoring always goes through Editorial Workflow, regardless of this option.
publish_mode.markdownDescription: Publish mode for the collection. This overrides the global `publish_mode` option, so Editorial Workflow can be enabled for some collections only, or turned off for a collection when it’s enabled globally. In the object form, each option overrides the global one of the same name, and the others are inherited. Default: global `publish_mode` option value. Note that a contributor working on a fork with Open Authoring always goes through Editorial Workflow, regardless of this option.

publish.description: Whether to show the publishing control UI for Editorial Workflow and Preview Workflow. Default: `true`. Set this to `false` to let editors move an entry through the review stages without being able to publish it themselves. It has no effect unless the `editorial_workflow` or `preview` publish mode is enabled.
publish.markdownDescription: Whether to show the publishing control UI for Editorial Workflow and Preview Workflow. Default: `true`. Set this to `false` to let editors move an entry through the review stages without being able to publish it themselves. It has no effect unless the `editorial_workflow` or `preview` publish mode is enabled.

format.description: File format. It should match the file extension. Default: detected from the file extension: `frontmatter` for Markdown files like `.md`, which reads YAML, TOML or JSON front matter and writes YAML front matter, `yaml` for `.yml`/`.yaml`, `toml` for `.toml`, `json` for `.json`, `raw` for `.astro`, and `yaml-frontmatter` otherwise.
format.markdownDescription: File format. It should match the file extension. Default: detected from the file extension: `frontmatter` for Markdown files like `.md`, which reads YAML, TOML or JSON front matter and writes YAML front matter, `yaml` for `.yml`/`.yaml`, `toml` for `.toml`, `json` for `.json`, `raw` for `.astro`, and `yaml-frontmatter` otherwise.

frontmatter_delimiter.description: Delimiters to be used for the front matter format. Default: depends on the front matter type.
frontmatter_delimiter.markdownDescription: Delimiters to be used for the front matter format. Default: depends on the front matter type.

body_field.description: Body field options for front matter formats.
body_field.markdownDescription: Body field options for front matter formats.

i18n.description: I18n options. Default: `false`.
i18n.markdownDescription: I18n options. Default: `false`.

preview_path.description: Preview URL path template, appended to the site URL or the deploy preview URL to link to the entry. Without it, a published entry has no link, while an unpublished Editorial Workflow entry links to the root of its deploy preview. For a file collection, define it on each file instead. See the [documentation](https://sveltiacms.app/en/docs/workflows/deploy-previews) for details.
preview_path.markdownDescription: Preview URL path template, appended to the site URL or the deploy preview URL to link to the entry. Without it, a published entry has no link, while an unpublished Editorial Workflow entry links to the root of its deploy preview. For a file collection, define it on each file instead. See the [documentation](https://sveltiacms.app/en/docs/workflows/deploy-previews) for details.

preview_path_date_field.description: Name of a top-level DateTime field used to fill the date and time tags in `preview_path`. Default: the first DateTime field. For a file collection, define it on each file instead.
preview_path_date_field.markdownDescription: Name of a top-level DateTime field used to fill the date and time tags in `preview_path`. Default: the first DateTime field. For a file collection, define it on each file instead.

yaml_quote.description: Whether to double-quote all the strings values if the YAML format is used for file output. Default: `false`.
yaml_quote.markdownDescription: Whether to double-quote all the strings values if the YAML format is used for file output. Default: `false`.
yaml_quote.deprecationMessage: Use the global YAML format options. `yaml_quote: true` is equivalent to `output.yaml.quote: double`. See the documentation https://sveltiacms.app/en/docs/data-output#controlling-data-output for details.

name.description: Unique identifier for the collection.
name.markdownDescription: Unique identifier for the collection.

label.description: Label of the collection to be displayed in the editor UI. Default: `name` option value.
label.markdownDescription: Label of the collection to be displayed in the editor UI. Default: `name` option value.

icon.description: Name of a [Material Symbols icon](https://fonts.google.com/icons?icon.set=Material+Symbols) to be displayed in the collection list.
icon.markdownDescription: Name of a [Material Symbols icon](https://fonts.google.com/icons?icon.set=Material+Symbols) to be displayed in the collection list.

readonly.description: Whether to make the collection read-only. Default: `false`. Its entries or files can be viewed but not created, edited, duplicated, reordered, deleted or moved through the Editorial Workflow stages, and assets can’t be uploaded to, changed or deleted from its media folders. For an asset collection, assets can’t be uploaded to, changed or deleted from the folder. It’s also read-only if the global `readonly` option is `true`. For a file collection, each file can also be made read-only with its own `readonly` option.
readonly.markdownDescription: Whether to make the collection read-only. Default: `false`. Its entries or files can be viewed but not created, edited, duplicated, reordered, deleted or moved through the Editorial Workflow stages, and assets can’t be uploaded to, changed or deleted from its media folders. For an asset collection, assets can’t be uploaded to, changed or deleted from the folder. It’s also read-only if the global `readonly` option is `true`. For a file collection, each file can also be made read-only with its own `readonly` option.

EntryCollection.description: Entry collection definition. In Netlify/Decap CMS, an entry collection is called a folder collection.
EntryCollection.markdownDescription: Entry collection definition. In Netlify/Decap CMS, an entry collection is called a folder collection.

StandardField.description: Entry field using a built-in field type.
StandardField.markdownDescription: Entry field using a built-in field type.

before_input.description: An extra label to be displayed before the input UI. Markdown is supported. Default: empty string.
before_input.markdownDescription: An extra label to be displayed before the input UI. Markdown is supported. Default: empty string.

after_input.description: An extra label to be displayed after the input UI. Markdown is supported. Default: empty string.
after_input.markdownDescription: An extra label to be displayed after the input UI. Markdown is supported. Default: empty string.

default.description: Default value. Accepts `true` or `false`. Default: `false`.
default.markdownDescription: Default value. Accepts `true` or `false`. Default: `false`.

default_localized.description: Default values for specific locales, keyed by locale code. A value given for a locale takes precedence over `default` in that locale. See the [documentation](https://sveltiacms.app/en/docs/i18n/options#localized-field-options) for details.
default_localized.markdownDescription: Default values for specific locales, keyed by locale code. A value given for a locale takes precedence over `default` in that locale. See the [documentation](https://sveltiacms.app/en/docs/i18n/options#localized-field-options) for details.

hint.description: Help message to be displayed below the input UI. Limited Markdown formatting is supported: bold, italic, strikethrough, inline code and links. A line break can be given as a literal backslash followed by `n`, e.g. `\n` in a plain or single-quoted YAML string; in JSON or a double-quoted string, the backslash itself has to be escaped. The hint is not displayed while the field is read-only.
hint.markdownDescription: Help message to be displayed below the input UI. Limited Markdown formatting is supported: bold, italic, strikethrough, inline code and links. A line break can be given as a literal backslash followed by `n`, e.g. `\n` in a plain or single-quoted YAML string; in JSON or a double-quoted string, the backslash itself has to be escaped. The hint is not displayed while the field is read-only.

hint_localized.description: Help messages for specific locales, keyed by locale code, taking precedence over `hint`. See the [documentation](https://sveltiacms.app/en/docs/i18n/options#localized-field-options) for details.
hint_localized.markdownDescription: Help messages for specific locales, keyed by locale code, taking precedence over `hint`. See the [documentation](https://sveltiacms.app/en/docs/i18n/options#localized-field-options) for details.

preview.description: Whether to show the preview of the field. Default: `true`.
preview.markdownDescription: Whether to show the preview of the field. Default: `true`.

required.description: Whether to make data input on the field required. Default: `true`. This option also affects data output if the `omit_empty_optional_fields` global output option is `true`. If i18n is enabled and the field doesn’t require input in all locales, required locale codes can be passed as an array like `[en, fr]` instead of a boolean.
required.markdownDescription: Whether to make data input on the field required. Default: `true`. This option also affects data output if the `omit_empty_optional_fields` global output option is `true`. If i18n is enabled and the field doesn’t require input in all locales, required locale codes can be passed as an array like `[en, fr]` instead of a boolean.

readonly.description: Whether to make the field read-only. Default: `false`, or `true` for the UUID field type. This is useful when a `default` value is provided and the field should not be editable by users.
readonly.markdownDescription: Whether to make the field read-only. Default: `false`, or `true` for the UUID field type. This is useful when a `default` value is provided and the field should not be editable by users.

i18n.description: Whether to enable the editor UI in locales other than the default locale. Default: `false`, or `duplicate` for a subfield of a field using `duplicate`. `duplicate` makes the field read-only in non-default locales and automatically copies the default locale’s value to them. `translate` and `none` are aliases of `true` and `false`, respectively. This option only works when i18n is set up with the global and collection-level `i18n` option. See the [documentation](https://sveltiacms.app/en/docs/i18n/options#field-level-configuration) for details.
i18n.markdownDescription: Whether to enable the editor UI in locales other than the default locale. Default: `false`, or `duplicate` for a subfield of a field using `duplicate`. `duplicate` makes the field read-only in non-default locales and automatically copies the default locale’s value to them. `translate` and `none` are aliases of `true` and `false`, respectively. This option only works when i18n is set up with the global and collection-level `i18n` option. See the [documentation](https://sveltiacms.app/en/docs/i18n/options#field-level-configuration) for details.

name.description: Unique identifier for the field among its sibling fields. It cannot contain spaces, periods, asterisks, colons or angle brackets.
name.markdownDescription: Unique identifier for the field among its sibling fields. It cannot contain spaces, periods, asterisks, colons or angle brackets.

label.description: Label of the field to be displayed in the editor UI. Default: `name` field value.
label.markdownDescription: Label of the field to be displayed in the editor UI. Default: `name` field value.

label_localized.description: Labels for specific locales, keyed by locale code, taking precedence over `label`. The editor shows the label for the locale being edited; elsewhere, the label for the UI locale is used. See the [documentation](https://sveltiacms.app/en/docs/i18n/options#localized-field-options) for details.
label_localized.markdownDescription: Labels for specific locales, keyed by locale code, taking precedence over `label`. The editor shows the label for the locale being edited; elsewhere, the label for the UI locale is used. See the [documentation](https://sveltiacms.app/en/docs/i18n/options#localized-field-options) for details.

comment.description: Comment to be written before the field in a YAML file or YAML front matter, for developers reading the file. It’s not displayed in the editor UI; use `hint` for that. A line break can be given as `\n`. The comment on a subfield of an Object field is written before the subfield, while the one on a subfield of a List field or a variable-type Object field is ignored. TOML and JSON files don’t support comments.
comment.markdownDescription: Comment to be written before the field in a YAML file or YAML front matter, for developers reading the file. It’s not displayed in the editor UI; use `hint` for that. A line break can be given as `\n`. The comment on a subfield of an Object field is written before the subfield, while the one on a subfield of a List field or a variable-type Object field is ignored. TOML and JSON files don’t support comments.

default.description: Default value. It must be a string if `output_code_only` is `true`. Otherwise it should be an object that matches the `keys` option, like `{ code: 'let x = 1;', lang: 'js' }`; a string is used as the code.
default.markdownDescription: Default value. It must be a string if `output_code_only` is `true`. Otherwise it should be an object that matches the `keys` option, like `{ code: 'let x = 1;', lang: 'js' }`; a string is used as the code.

default_localized.description: Default values for specific locales, keyed by locale code. A value given for a locale takes precedence over `default` in that locale. See the [documentation](https://sveltiacms.app/en/docs/i18n/options#localized-field-options) for details.
default_localized.markdownDescription: Default values for specific locales, keyed by locale code. A value given for a locale takes precedence over `default` in that locale. See the [documentation](https://sveltiacms.app/en/docs/i18n/options#localized-field-options) for details.

default_language.description: Default language to be selected, like `js`. See the [Shiki documentation](https://shiki.style/languages) for a list of supported languages. Default: empty string, which is plaintext.
default_language.markdownDescription: Default language to be selected, like `js`. See the [Shiki documentation](https://shiki.style/languages) for a list of supported languages. Default: empty string, which is plaintext.

allow_language_selection.description: Whether to show a language switcher so that users can change the language mode. Default: `true` (the Decap CMS document is wrong).
allow_language_selection.markdownDescription: Whether to show a language switcher so that users can change the language mode. Default: `true` (the Decap CMS document is wrong).

output_code_only.description: Whether to save the code only, as a string, instead of an object containing the code and the language. Default: `false`.
output_code_only.markdownDescription: Whether to save the code only, as a string, instead of an object containing the code and the language. Default: `false`.

keys.description: Output property names. It has no effect if `output_code_only` is `true`. Default: `{ code: 'code', lang: 'lang' }`.
keys.markdownDescription: Output property names. It has no effect if `output_code_only` is `true`. Default: `{ code: 'code', lang: 'lang' }`.

pattern.description: Validation format. The first argument is a regular expression matching pattern for a valid input value, and the second argument is an error message to be displayed when the input value does not match the pattern.

i18n.description: Whether to enable the editor UI in locales other than the default locale. Default: `false`, or `duplicate` for a subfield of a field using `duplicate`. `duplicate` makes the field read-only in non-default locales and automatically copies the default locale’s value to them. `duplicate_if_empty` copies the default locale’s value to non-default locales only where the value is empty, or still the same as the default locale’s value, while the field can be edited in every locale. It’s not supported for a File or Image field that accepts multiple files. `translate` and `none` are aliases of `true` and `false`, respectively. This option only works when i18n is set up with the global and collection-level `i18n` option. See the [documentation](https://sveltiacms.app/en/docs/i18n/options#field-level-configuration) for details.

unique.description: Whether the value must be different from the value of the same field in every other entry of the collection, like a `UNIQUE` constraint in a relational database. An empty value is not checked; combine it with `required: true` to make sure every entry has a distinct value. Only available in an entry collection, and ignored for a field that takes multiple values, or a field in a List field or a rich text editor component. A Color field value is compared regardless of case, a Number field value by its numeric value, and a File or Image field value just uploaded isn’t compared, as it’s a new file. Default: `false`.

value.description: Value template, like `posts-{{fields.slug}}`. Besides the `fields.*` tags, which support transformations like `{{fields.title | upper}}`, `{{index}}` is the position of the item in a list, which is saved as a number when used alone, and `{{uuid}}`, `{{uuid_short}}` and `{{uuid_shorter}}` generate a UUID, which is kept once the value is saved. In a list item, a `*` in a `fields.*` tag stands for the current item, so `{{fields.lines.*.price}}` is the price of the item the field is in. With a numeric `value_type`, it’s an arithmetic expression instead, like `{{fields.price}} * {{fields.quantity}}`, which can have numbers, template tags other than the UUID tags, the `+`, `-`, `*`, `/` and `%` operators, parentheses, the `abs`, `ceil`, `floor` and `round` functions and the `avg`, `count`, `max`, `min` and `sum` aggregate functions, in which the last `*` of a tag stands for every item of the list, like `sum({{fields.lines.*.amount}})`, and empty values are left out. The field is always hidden in the editor, and its value can’t be edited.

value_type.description: Type of the value. `string` makes the `value` option a template and saves the result as a string. The other types make it an arithmetic expression: `int` and `float` save the result as an integer or a floating-point number, respectively, and `int/string` and `float/string` save it as a string. An integer is rounded to the nearest one, and the result is left empty if a template tag resolves to an empty value or something other than a number. Default: `string`.
